## 9. Non-Functional Requirements

requirements.title: Portability
requirements.statement: Airframe Core shall be designed as a reusable package or library usable by both UI and CLI clients.

requirements.title: Maintainability
requirements.statement: Airframe Core shall separate domain model, workflow policy, authority evaluation, backend adapters, metrics, audit, and configuration concerns.

requirements.title: Testability
requirements.statement: Airframe Core shall support unit tests, mock backend tests, policy tests, workflow transition tests, and metrics tests.

requirements.title: Performance
requirements.statement: Airframe Core shall support efficient dashboard and task-packet generation without requiring unnecessary full-project context loading.

requirements.title: Reliability
requirements.statement: Airframe Core shall handle backend errors, stale data, invalid transitions, authorization failures, and configuration errors predictably.

requirements.title: Extensibility
requirements.statement: Airframe Core shall support adding backend adapters, entity types, metrics, and policy rules without requiring changes to client CSCIs.

requirements.title: Token Efficiency
requirements.statement:
Airframe Core shall support generation of compact summaries and task packets to reduce LLM token usage.

---

## 10. Verification Requirements

requirements.title: Deny by Default
requirements.statement: Airframe Core shall deny operations when actor identity, actor type, project context, target project, operation permission, or workflow state cannot be certified.

requirements.title: Credential Scope Validation
requirements.statement: Airframe Core shall validate credential scope before permitting write operations.

requirements.title: No Self-Declared Authority
requirements.statement: Airframe Core shall not trust caller-provided authority class, actor type, or project scope unless derived from trusted credential context or configuration.

requirements.title: Project-Scoped Mutation
requirements.statement: Airframe Core shall only allow mutation of entities belonging to the actor's certified execution project unless explicit cross-project delegation exists.

requirements.title: Cross-Project Delegation
requirements.statement: Airframe Core shall support explicit, narrow, auditable cross-project delegation policies.

requirements.title: Human-Only Operation Enforcement
requirements.statement: Airframe Core shall prevent non-human actors from performing human-only operations.

requirements.title: Sensitive Operation Policy
requirements.statement: Airframe Core shall support policy requirements for confirmation or additional checks before sensitive operations.

requirements.title: Audit Trail Integrity
requirements.statement:
Airframe Core shall generate audit events that identify actor, actor type, execution project, target project, operation, result, reason code, target entity, backend reference, and timestamp where available.

---

## 5. Data Requirements

requirements.title: Domain Model Tests
requirements.statement: Tests shall verify canonical entity creation, validation, serialization, and mapping.

requirements.title: Task Packet Data
requirements.statement: AI Cockpit shall consume task packet data generated or assembled by Airframe Core.

requirements.title: Entity Proposal Data
requirements.statement: AI Cockpit shall provide proposal data for issues and tasks using Airframe Core canonical fields.

requirements.title: Evidence Data
requirements.statement: AI Cockpit shall support evidence records containing summary, source, timestamp, command results, file references, and optional backend references.

requirements.title: Output Data Minimization
requirements.statement:
AI Cockpit shall minimize output to the data required for the requested operation unless verbose output is explicitly requested.

## 6. Interface Requirements

requirements.title: Command-Line Interface
requirements.statement: AI Cockpit shall provide a command-line interface for project-management operations.

requirements.title: Project Context Discovery
requirements.statement: AI Cockpit shall determine the execution project from Airframe Core-certified context, configuration, or credential scope.

requirements.title: Propose Issue
requirements.statement: AI Cockpit shall allow authorized LLM agents to propose issues within their certified project context.

requirements.title: Propose Task
requirements.statement: AI Cockpit shall allow authorized LLM agents to propose tasks within their certified project context.

requirements.title: Retrieve Next Task
requirements.statement: AI Cockpit shall support retrieval of the next task appropriate to the agent's execution project and authority.

requirements.title: Generate Task Packet
requirements.statement:
AI Cockpit shall generate compact task packets containing:

- Project name.
- Work item identifier.
- Objective.
- Scope.
- Out-of-scope constraints.
- Acceptance criteria.
- Verification requirements.
- Relevant files, when available.
- Protected paths or no-touch areas.
- Required final report format.

requirements.title: Attach Evidence
requirements.statement: AI Cockpit shall allow authorized agents to attach evidence to a work item, including command output summaries, test results, changed files, or implementation notes.

requirements.title: Mark Ready for Human Verification
requirements.statement: AI Cockpit shall allow authorized agents to request transition of a work item to Ready for Human Verification when Airframe Core permits the transition.

requirements.title: Project Summary
requirements.statement: AI Cockpit shall support compact project summary output for the execution project.

requirements.title: Multi-Project Summary Restrictions
requirements.statement: AI Cockpit shall not allow an LLM agent to retrieve or mutate multi-project data unless the actor has explicit authority or read-only aggregation permission.

requirements.title: Deny Human-Only Operations
requirements.statement: AI Cockpit shall deny attempts by LLM agents to accept work, reject work as final, close issues, open or close sprints, open or close epics, approve architecture decisions, or change workflow rules.

requirements.title: Project Scope Mismatch Detection
requirements.statement: AI Cockpit shall detect and report project scope mismatches returned by Airframe Core.

requirements.title: Structured Output
requirements.statement: AI Cockpit shall support structured output formats suitable for LLM consumption, including Markdown and JSON.

requirements.title: Dry-Run Mode
requirements.statement: AI Cockpit should support a dry-run mode that validates an operation without committing backend changes.

requirements.title: Audit Display
requirements.statement:
AI Cockpit shall display or return audit identifiers for write operations where available.

---

## 4. Security and Authority Requirements

requirements.title: Airframe Core API
requirements.statement: AI Cockpit shall use Airframe Core APIs for all project-management operations.

requirements.title: CLI Command Model
requirements.statement: AI Cockpit commands shall use domain terms such as issue, task, evidence, verification, sprint, and epic rather than backend-specific names.

requirements.title: Machine-Readable Output
requirements.statement: AI Cockpit shall provide machine-readable output suitable for LLM or automation consumption.

requirements.title: Error Output
requirements.statement: AI Cockpit shall provide concise, structured error output including reason codes for denied operations.

requirements.title: Configuration Interface
requirements.statement:
AI Cockpit shall load project and actor context using Airframe Core-defined configuration mechanisms.

---

## 7. Non-Functional Requirements

requirements.title: Token Efficiency
requirements.statement: AI Cockpit shall be optimized to reduce LLM token consumption by returning compact, relevant, task-specific information.

requirements.title: Deterministic Output
requirements.statement: AI Cockpit output shall be deterministic for a given request and system state, excluding timestamps or backend-generated identifiers.

requirements.title: Portability
requirements.statement: AI Cockpit shall operate in local development environments used by coding agents and automation workflows.

requirements.title: Reliability
requirements.statement: AI Cockpit shall clearly distinguish backend failures, authentication failures, authorization failures, invalid workflow transitions, and project scope mismatches.

requirements.title: Maintainability
requirements.statement:
AI Cockpit shall keep command parsing and output formatting separate from Airframe Core authority and workflow logic.

---

## 8. Verification Requirements

requirements.title: Certified Agent Identity
requirements.statement: AI Cockpit shall rely on Airframe Core to authenticate and certify the actor identity and actor type.

requirements.title: No Actor Spoofing
requirements.statement: AI Cockpit shall not accept command-line flags or input fields that grant or override actor type, role, or authority.

requirements.title: Project-Scoped Authority
requirements.statement: AI Cockpit shall enforce Airframe Core's project-scoped authority decisions. An agent running under project X shall not mutate project Z unless explicit cross-project delegation exists.

requirements.title: Credential Scope Validation
requirements.statement: AI Cockpit shall provide credential context to Airframe Core when required to validate operation scope.

requirements.title: Deny by Default
requirements.statement: AI Cockpit shall deny operations when identity, actor type, project context, target project, or workflow state cannot be certified.

requirements.title: Human-Only Gate Protection
requirements.statement: AI Cockpit shall not provide bypass mechanisms for human-only workflow gates.

requirements.title: Auditability
requirements.statement:
All AI Cockpit write operations shall result in Airframe Core-generated audit events.

---

## 5. Data Requirements

requirements.title: Command Tests
requirements.statement: Tests shall verify AI Cockpit command parsing and output formatting.

requirements.title: Authority Denial Tests
requirements.statement: Tests shall verify that LLM agents cannot perform human-only operations.

requirements.title: Project Scope Tests
requirements.statement: Tests shall verify that an agent operating under one project context cannot mutate another project without explicit delegation.

requirements.title: Task Packet Tests
requirements.statement: Tests shall verify that task packets contain required sections and omit unrelated context.

requirements.title: Evidence Tests
requirements.statement: Tests shall verify that evidence can be attached only to authorized target work items.

requirements.title: Output Format Tests
requirements.statement:
Tests shall verify Markdown and JSON output formats.

## 9. Open Issues

- Final CLI command names remain to be selected.
- Initial credential strategy for local LLM agents remains to be selected.
- Initial backend adapter is expected to be GitHub, but AI Cockpit shall remain backend-agnostic through Airframe Core.

requirements.title: Canonical Repo-Local Store
requirements.statement:
Airframe shall maintain canonical workflow state in a repo-local structured store.

Rationale: workflow state must move with the source code across branches, forks, checkouts, and reverts.

requirements.title: Stable Work Item Identity
requirements.statement: Airframe shall assign stable IDs to Epics, Sprints, Tasks, Issues, Requirements, Evidence records, and Trace records.

requirements.title: Relationship Model
requirements.statement:
Airframe shall represent relationships between work products by ID, including:

- Epic to Sprint.
- Epic to Task.
- Epic to Issue.
- Sprint to Task.
- Sprint to Issue.
- Requirement to Task.
- Requirement to Test.
- Requirement to Evidence.
- Task or Issue to Evidence.
- Work item to GitHub issue where applicable.

requirements.title: Workflow Policy Authority
requirements.statement: AirframeCore shall own workflow status definitions, allowed transitions, preconditions, and authority checks.

requirements.title: Markdown Projection
requirements.statement:
Airframe shall support generating human-readable Markdown documentation from canonical records.

Markdown projections shall not be the sole source of workflow truth.

requirements.title: Validation Diagnostics
requirements.statement:
AirframeCore shall detect inconsistent workflow state and report diagnostics with:

- Severity.
- Affected IDs.
- Reason code.
- Explanation.
- Recommended repair options.
- Required authority for repair.

requirements.title: Repair Preview
requirements.statement: Airframe shall support previewing proposed repair actions before applying them.

requirements.title: Audit Events
requirements.statement: Airframe shall record audit events for canonical state mutations, including actor, operation, affected IDs, before state, after state, and authority decision.

requirements.title: Test Evidence Summary
requirements.statement:
Airframe shall support recording summarized test evidence without storing every raw local test run.

At minimum, test evidence shall include:

- Command or test source.
- Pass/fail summary.
- Relevant failing tests when applicable.
- Timestamp.
- Environment summary.
- Linked requirement IDs when applicable.
- Optional CI run or artifact link.

requirements.title: CI Evidence Link
requirements.statement:
Airframe shall support linking verification evidence to CI runs or CI artifacts when CI is configured.

CI evidence shall supplement, not replace, AirframeCore requirement verification policy.

requirements.title: Requirement Traceability
requirements.statement: Airframe shall support traceability between requirements, implementation work, tests, evidence, and release decisions.

requirements.title: Fluid Requirements
requirements.statement: Airframe shall support requirement changes during development, including created, revised, superseded, deferred, waived, and removed requirement states.

requirements.title: External Import Export Stubs
requirements.statement:
Airframe shall reserve interfaces for importing and exporting requirements from external tools.

Version 1.0 shall prioritize diffable local formats such as CSV and JSON. DOORS integration shall remain out of scope for Version 1.0 but shall not be precluded by the data model.

requirements.title: Release Candidate Gate
requirements.statement: Airframe shall support release candidate close criteria based on workflow state, requirement traceability, verification evidence, validation approval, deviations, and blocking Issues.

requirements.title: Generated Compliance Outputs
requirements.statement:
Airframe shall support generating compliance and traceability documents from canonical records when templates are available.

Candidate outputs include:

- Compliance Verification Matrix.
- Requirements Traceability Matrix.
- Bidirectional Requirements Traceability Matrix.
- Deviation or waiver report.
- Test plan.
- Verification report.
- Release candidate closeout package.

## 4. Non-Functional Requirements

requirements.title: Diffability
requirements.statement: Canonical local state should be reasonably diffable in Git.

requirements.title: Human Inspectability
requirements.statement: Canonical state should be inspectable by humans using common repository tools.

requirements.title: Deterministic Projection
requirements.statement: Generated documentation should be deterministic to avoid noisy diffs.

requirements.title: Backward Compatibility
requirements.statement: Existing Markdown artifacts shall remain importable during migration.

requirements.title: Authority Preservation
requirements.statement:
Human-only verification, Sprint closure, Epic closure, release closeout, destructive repair, and policy mutation shall remain protected by AirframeCore authority evaluation.

## 5. Version 1.0 Boundary

Version 1.0 should include:

- Canonical repo-local state model.
- Basic requirement records.
- Requirement-to-work and requirement-to-test trace links.
- Summary test evidence.
- CI evidence link fields.
- CSV and JSON requirement import/export.
- Generated Markdown projections.
- Data health diagnostics.
- Initial AgileCockpit release gate visibility.

Version 1.0 should not include:

- Native DOORS integration.
- Full enterprise requirements management.
- Full document-template authoring.
- Server-based synchronization.
- Mandated code comments for every requirement.

requirements.title: Requirement Records
requirements.statement: Airframe shall maintain canonical requirement records with stable IDs.

requirements.title: Requirement Revision State
requirements.statement: Airframe shall support requirement revision metadata, including status, source, version, rationale, and change history.

requirements.title: Fluid Requirement Lifecycle
requirements.statement:
Airframe shall support requirement lifecycle states suitable for active development, including:

- Proposed.
- Draft.
- Active.
- Implemented.
- Verified.
- Validated.
- Deferred.
- Waived.
- Superseded.
- Removed.

requirements.title: Requirement Source
requirements.statement: Airframe shall record whether a requirement was authored in Airframe, imported from a file, imported from an external tool, generated from another artifact, or manually entered.

requirements.title: Implementation Trace
requirements.statement: Airframe shall support linking requirements to Tasks, Issues, Epics, Sprints, design records, source references, and commits where available.

requirements.title: Verification Trace
requirements.statement: Airframe shall support linking requirements to test cases, test results, manual verification records, CI runs, and evidence artifacts.

requirements.title: Validation Trace
requirements.statement: Airframe shall support linking requirements to human validation decisions and stakeholder approval evidence.

requirements.title: Bidirectional Traceability
requirements.statement:
Airframe shall support queries in both directions:

- From a requirement to implementing work, tests, evidence, and code references.
- From work, tests, evidence, and code references back to requirements.

requirements.title: Traceability Gap Detection
requirements.statement:
AirframeCore shall detect missing or incomplete traceability for in-scope requirements.

Example gaps:

- Requirement has no implementing work.
- Requirement has no verification method.
- Requirement has no passing verification evidence.
- Requirement has verification evidence but no validation decision where validation is required.
- Source reference claims a requirement that does not exist.

requirements.title: Release Scope
requirements.statement: Airframe shall support defining which requirements are in scope for a release candidate.

requirements.title: Release Gate Summary
requirements.statement:
AgileCockpit shall show release candidate close criteria, including:

- In-scope requirements count.
- Implemented requirements count.
- Verified requirements count.
- Validated requirements count.
- Deferred or waived requirements count.
- Open deviations.
- Blocking traceability gaps.
- Blocking Issues.
- Missing test evidence.
- Missing human approvals.

requirements.title: Deviation And Waiver Records
requirements.statement: Airframe shall support deviation and waiver records linked to affected requirements, rationale, authority, release scope, and expiration or review conditions.

requirements.title: Test Result Summaries
requirements.statement:
Airframe shall support storing summarized test result records that link to requirements.

Raw test logs may be external artifacts or CI artifacts and do not need to be committed to the repository.

requirements.title: CI Integration Link
requirements.statement: Airframe shall support optional CI links for test results, coverage results, build results, and release candidate evidence.

requirements.title: Code Reference Trace
requirements.statement:
Airframe shall support optional code-level trace references to requirements.

Supported references may include:

- Source comments.
- Test names.
- Test metadata.
- Work item records.
- Commit metadata.
- Generated source scans.

Airframe shall not require every requirement to be referenced directly in code comments unless project policy requires it.

requirements.title: Compliance Document Generation
requirements.statement:
Airframe shall support generating traceability and compliance documents from canonical records and templates.

Initial document targets:

- Compliance Verification Matrix.
- Requirements Traceability Matrix.
- Bidirectional Requirements Traceability Matrix.
- Deviation or waiver report.
- Test plan.
- Verification report.
- Release candidate closeout report.

## 4. Import Export Requirements

requirements.title: CSV Import
requirements.statement: Airframe shall support importing requirements from CSV.

requirements.title: CSV Export
requirements.statement: Airframe shall support exporting requirements and traceability summaries to CSV.

requirements.title: JSON Import Export
requirements.statement: Airframe shall support importing and exporting canonical requirement records as JSON.

requirements.title: Diffable Workflow
requirements.statement: Requirement import/export files shall support review through Git diffs where practical.

requirements.title: External Tool Stubs
requirements.statement:
Airframe shall reserve import/export adapter boundaries for external requirements tools such as DOORS.

Native DOORS integration is out of scope for Version 1.0.

## 5. Release Gate Requirements

requirements.title: Configurable Gate Policy
requirements.statement: AirframeCore shall support configurable release gate policy.

requirements.title: Default Gate Policy
requirements.statement:
The default release candidate gate shall require:

- No blocking Issues.
- All in-scope requirements are implemented, deferred, waived, or explicitly out of scope.
- All in-scope non-deferred requirements have required verification evidence.
- All requirements requiring validation have validation approval.
- All deviations and waivers have approving authority.
- No blocking traceability diagnostics remain.

requirements.title: Gate Explanation
requirements.statement: AirframeCore shall explain why a release candidate can or cannot close.

requirements.title: Human Authority
requirements.statement:
Final release candidate closeout and validation approval shall require human authority.

## 6. Version 1.0 Boundary

Version 1.0 should provide a lightweight traceability foundation:

- Requirement records.
- CSV/JSON import/export.
- Requirement-to-work trace links.
- Requirement-to-test trace links.
- Test evidence summaries.
- Release gate summary.
- Generated traceability reports from simple templates.

Version 1.0 should avoid:

- Full DOORS replacement behavior.
- Deep external requirements-tool synchronization.
- Mandatory source-code annotation for all requirements.
- Heavy template authoring workflows.

workItem.title: AgileCockpit Sprint and Epic Status Controls

epics.rationale: The current product still has live GitHub and controlled-remote paths. Those paths are useful, but they are not acceptable as a requirement for basic operation. Airframe must be able to load, inspect, mutate, verify, and archive work completely offline using local data only.
scope: Audit all runtime paths in AirframeCore, AICockpit, and AgileCockpit for hidden GitHub or network dependencies.
Ensure the local filesystem backend is sufficient for day-to-day project operation.
Make the CLI usable against a purely local workspace without requiring GitHub authentication or network access.
Make AgileCockpit usable against a purely local workspace without requiring GitHub authentication or network access.
Preserve existing GitHub-backed functionality as optional, not required.
Add offline regression coverage for project load, dashboard display, task packets, verification, planning, and archive updates.
outOfScope: Building a network server or sync service.
Replacing the local filesystem backend with a new storage engine.
notes: Acceptance Criteria: 1. Airframe can launch and operate with only the local filesystem backend configured. 2. AICockpit can read, create, update, and transition supported work items offline. 3. AgileCockpit can load the dashboard, review view, planning view, and verification flows offline. 4. Sprint and Epic workflows do not require GitHub access or any remote server for core local operation. 5. Offline regression tests pass without network access or GitHub credentials. 6. GitHub-backed paths remain optional and do not block local workflows when unavailable.

Implementation Plan: 1. Inventory all code paths that assume GitHub availability or a remote backend. 2. Separate local-first behavior from optional live-GitHub behavior in AirframeCore and the two client apps. 3. Add explicit offline-mode tests for AICockpit and AgileCockpit against local fixture data. 4. Harden configuration and failure messaging so missing GitHub credentials do not break local usage. 5. Verify that all essential workflows continue to work entirely from the local workspace, including archive and status updates.
Related Areas: - `AirframeCore` - `AICockpit` - `AgileCockpit` - `docs/Tasks/` - `docs/Issues/` - `docs/Sprints/` - `docs/Epics/`

Notes: - This Epic is about survivable product operation, not just “offline-friendly” fallback behavior. - If a feature cannot operate without GitHub or a server, it should be explicitly marked optional rather than assumed.
epics.goal: Make Airframe fully functional without GitHub or any backend server so the workspace, CLI, and app can operate entirely offline against local files and local state.

workItem.title: Airframe Offline-Only Operation

epics.rationale: EP-018 exposed that Markdown artifacts currently act as both human-readable documentation and mutable canonical state. That made Airframe vulnerable to inconsistent states where an Epic, Sprint, Task, Issue, index, workspace configuration, and GitHub label disagreed. Airframe now owns a canonical repo-local state model in AirframeCore so workflow state evolves with the source code and remains valid across branches, forks, checkouts, reverts, and release tags.
outOfScope: Native DOORS or enterprise requirements-tool integration.
Compliance document generation beyond schema stubs and projection groundwork.
Removing existing Markdown artifacts before migration and projection behavior is verified.
Making GitHub Issues the canonical source of Airframe workflow state.
notes: Scope Completed: - Canonical AirframeCore record models were defined for Workspace, Project, Epic, Sprint, Task, Issue, acceptance criteria, evidence summaries, audit events, backend mappings, workflow definitions, and workflow transitions. - The repo-local structured store was implemented as one JSON file per canonical record kind. - Epic, Sprint, Task, and Issue workflow policies were encoded in AirframeCore instead of relying on guideline Markdown as authority. - Validation diagnostics were added for active/backlog/closed inconsistencies, relationship drift, invalid configured active work, and unsupported human-only mutations. - Import support from the current Markdown artifacts into canonical records was added. - Deterministic Markdown projection support for human-readable documentation was added. - AICockpit now queries canonical records for discovery, summaries, and task packets. - AgileCockpit now reads canonical records for dashboard and planning views. - Human-only authority boundaries remain enforced for verification, Sprint closure, Epic closure, destructive repair, and policy mutation.

Acceptance Criteria: 1. [x] AirframeCore defines canonical Codable records for core work products, workflow policy, evidence summaries, and audit events. 2. [x] AirframeCore can load and validate a repo-local canonical workflow store. 3. [x] AirframeCore diagnostics detect invalid active/backlog/closed states and relationship drift. 4. [x] Existing Markdown work artifacts can be imported into canonical records with stable IDs preserved. 5. [x] Markdown documentation can be generated deterministically from canonical records. 6. [x] AICockpit reads project summaries and task packets from canonical records without reparsing Markdown as the primary state source. 7. [x] AgileCockpit dashboard and planning views can render from canonical records. 8. [x] Human-only transitions remain blocked outside human-authorized AgileCockpit workflows. 9. [x] Tests cover canonical load, validation, import, projection, and authority-preserving mutation behavior.
epics.goal: Move Airframe workflow state from Markdown-authored artifacts to AirframeCore-owned canonical structured records, with validation diagnostics, migration support, generated documentation projections, and repo-coupled history.

workItem.title: Canonical Airframe Workflow State

epics.rationale: Airframe work products must connect implementation, tests, evidence, requirements, and release decisions. CI can provide test artifacts and build evidence, but AirframeCore must understand whether in-scope requirements have been implemented, verified, validated, deferred, waived, or blocked. Requirements are fluid during development, so the model must support change and import/export while preserving repo-local development history.
scope: Define canonical requirement, requirement revision, trace link, test case, test result summary, deviation, waiver, release scope, and release gate records.
Support requirement lifecycle states including Proposed, Draft, Active, Implemented, Verified, Validated, Deferred, Waived, Superseded, and Removed.
Support traceability from requirements to Tasks, Issues, Epics, Sprints, tests, evidence, design records, source references, deviations, waivers, and release scopes.
Support summarized test evidence linked to requirements without committing every raw local test run.
Support optional links to CI runs, CI artifacts, build results, coverage results, and release candidate evidence.
Add CSV and JSON import/export for requirements and traceability data, with dry-run import previews.
Reserve adapter boundaries for future external requirements tools such as DOORS while keeping native DOORS integration out of Version 1.0.
Add AgileCockpit views for release candidate close criteria, traceability gaps, deviations, waivers, missing test evidence, and missing human approvals.

Add generated documentation support for Compliance Verification Matrix, Requirements Traceability Matrix, Bidirectional Requirements Traceability Matrix, deviation or waiver report, test plan, verification report, and release candidate closeout package when templates are available.
outOfScope: Mandatory code-comment traceability for every requirement.
Storing every raw local test run in the repository.
Final release closeout automation without human authority.
notes: Acceptance Criteria: 1. AirframeCore defines canonical records for requirements, revisions, trace links, test evidence summaries, deviations, waivers, release scopes, and release gates. 2. Requirements can be imported from and exported to CSV. 3. Requirements can be imported from and exported to canonical JSON. 4. Import dry runs report created, updated, unchanged, removed, and conflicted records before mutation. 5. AirframeCore can identify traceability gaps for in-scope requirements. 6. Test evidence summaries can link test outcomes to requirement IDs and optional CI artifacts. 7. AgileCockpit shows release candidate gate status, including implemented, verified, validated, deferred, waived, and blocked requirement counts. 8. AirframeCore can explain why a release candidate can or cannot close. 9. Generated traceability and compliance documents can be produced from canonical state using deterministic default layouts or provided templates. 10. Tests cover import/export, traceability diagnostics, release gate evaluation, and evidence-to-requirement linking.
epics.goal: Add lightweight repo-coupled requirements traceability, test evidence summaries, release candidate gate visibility, external import/export stubs, and generated compliance documentation support without turning Airframe into a replacement for DOORS.

issues.expectedBehavior: Airframe and Telemetrix should be able to run AgileCockpit at the same time as separate visible instances. Each instance should read and display only its own project-local workspace configuration and backend data.
notes: Description: Launching AgileCockpit from the Telemetrix project and then from the Airframe project could still show Telemetrix data, and an already running Telemetrix instance prevented a separate Airframe cockpit from being brought up independently.
Actual Behavior: The second launch could reuse or display the first project's data, and the app could not reliably present both projects on screen simultaneously.

Root Cause Analysis: The project-local launcher used `open --fresh` on the shared AgileCockpit bundle. Launch Services can still target the existing bundle identity, so the second project launch could reuse the already running app process instead of creating a separate process with the new project environment.
Resolution: The launcher now uses `open -n --fresh` so each project-local launch requests a new app instance with that launcher's `AIRFRAME_CONFIG_PATH` and `AIRFRAME_STORE_PATH`.

Files Affected: - `.airframe/scripts/ac-launch-cockpit.sh`: Added `-n` to force a new app instance for each project-local launch. - `../Telemetrix/.airframe/scripts/ac-launch-cockpit.sh`: Human applied the same `open -n --fresh` launcher fix. - `AgileCockpit/AgileCockpit/ContentView.swift`: Made project identity more visible so concurrent instances are easier to distinguish.
